## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to add observability with minimal surface area using existing CNF sidecars and Kubernetes ConfigMaps. It assesses understanding of multi-tenant security boundaries and metrics cardinality management.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant labeling in Prometheus metrics
- Prometheus text format exposition
- ConfigMap-based feature flags and sampling control
- High-cardinality label management

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-metrics-config
  namespace: tenant-namespace
data:
  cnf.metrics.enabled: 'true'
  cnf.metrics.endpoint: '/metrics'
  cnf.metrics.sample-rate: '0.5'
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-namespace
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-metrics-config
  namespace: tenant-namespace
data:
  cnf.metrics.enabled: 'true'
  cnf.metrics.endpoint: '/metrics'
  cnf.metrics.sample-rate: '0.5'
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-namespace
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: cnf-gateway:latest
      - name: metrics-sidecar
        image: metrics-sidecar:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
          name: metrics
```

- How would you handle high-cardinality label explosion with many tenants and paths?
- How would you verify no tenant data cross-contamination occurs in metrics?
- How does the sampling rate affect metric accuracy and Prometheus storage?

## Why This Is Asked
- Validates understanding of namespace-scoped quotas and limits, a core tenancy control pattern in multi-tenant Kubernetes environments.

## Key Concepts
- ResourceQuota: Enforces aggregate resource limits across a namespace
- LimitRange: Defines default requests/limits and validates pod resource specifications
- Per-namespace isolation: Ensures tenants cannot exceed allocated resources
- Quota enforcement: Kubernetes rejects pods that would exceed quota limits
- Validation methods: kubectl describe quota and limitrange commands

## Code Example
```yaml
# Namespace: cnf-tenant-A
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: cnf-tenant-A

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: cnf-tenant-A-quota
  namespace: cnf-tenant-A
spec:
  hard:
    limits.cpu: 4
    limits.memory: 16Gi
    requests.cpu: 2
    requests.memory: 8Gi

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: cnf-tenant-A-limits
  namespace: cnf-tenant-A
spec:
  limits:
  - default:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    type: Container
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical policy design at the intersection of CNF gateways, Kubernetes admission control, and SBOM-driven security. It requires translating per-tenant risk tolerances into enforceable constraints and verifying end-to-end behavior.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA integration for admission control
- Per-namespace configuration and binding
- SBOM-driven vulnerability data (CVSS) attached to images
- Rego-based enforcement logic and concise ConstraintTemplates
- End-to-end testing: apply templates, constraints, and verify allow/deny outcomes

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate: CNFImageVuln
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: cnfimagevuln
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: CNFImageVuln
      scope: Cluster
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package cnfimagevuln
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      # image.vulns is a list of {cve, cvss}
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        input.review.object.kind == "Deployment";
        ns := input.review.object.metadata.namespace;
        threshold := data.namespaceThresholds[ns];
        some i;
        vul := input.review.object.metadata.annotations["image.vulns"];
        cvss := vul[i].cvss;
        cvss > threshold; msg := sprintf("CVSS %v exceeds threshold %v for namespace %s", [cvss, threshold, ns]);
      }
```
```yaml
# Constraint: Bind per-namespace threshold
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: CNFImageVuln
metadata:
  name: cnf-image-vuln-namespace
spec:
  namespaceSelector:
    matchExpressions:
    - {key: "cnf.namespace", operator: In, values: ["default"]}
```
```yaml
# Test manifest: should fail for CVSS > threshold and pass otherwise
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test-cnf
  namespace: default
  annotations:
    image.vulns: "[{\"cve\":\"CVE-2024-0001\",\"cvss\":9}]"
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: test-cnf
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: test-cnf
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/cnf:latest
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle multi-tenant overrides for temporary risk surges?
- How would you test performance impact of SBOM parsing in high-scale deployments?

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests understanding of safe, per-tenant traffic experimentation without impacting production. It covers config-driven behavior, sidecar responsibilities, and end‑to‑end validation in a CNF gateway on Kubernetes.

## Key Concepts

- Traffic shadowing (mirroring) to a test shadow target
- Per-tenant configuration via Namespace ConfigMaps
- Fire-and-forget asynchronous forwards
- Deriving shadow path from tenant identity (X-TENANT-ID) and request path
- Observability: simple verification endpoint and metrics

## Code Example

```yaml
# Namespace ConfigMap (per-tenant) - cnf-shadow.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-shadow
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  cnf.shadow.enabled: "true"
  cnf.shadow.percent: "10"
  cnf.shadow.target: "shadow-svc.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local"
```

```yaml
# Minimal Deployment patch to mount config via envFrom (sidecar example)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: your/gateway:latest
      - name: sidecar-shadow
        image: your/cnf-shadow-sidecar:latest
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: cnf-shadow
```
